answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a voyage as the anchor of the cost.
